name: NIH parent announcements (investigator-initiated applications)
what: A [parent announcement](#term:parent-announcement) is a standing, broad [notice of funding opportunity (NOFO)](#term:nofo) that an applicant uses to send in an investigator-initiated application, one whose topic the investigator chose and [NIH](#term:nih) did not ask for [1](#cite:1) [145](#cite:145). Each parent announcement is for one [activity code](#term:activity-code), such as [R01](#term:r01), [R21](#term:r21-r03), R03 or [R15](#term:r15) [1](#cite:1). Every NIH application answers a specific NOFO, so an [unsolicited](#term:unsolicited-request) idea still goes in through one of these notices [120](#cite:120). During 2025 NIH cut the number of narrow notices and leaned more on parent announcements [90](#cite:90) [10](#cite:10).
status_note: The parent announcements page lists the research-project parents PA-25-301 and PA-25-305 (R01), PA-25-304 and PA-25-306 (R21), PA-25-302 (R03), PAR-25-134 and PAR-25-148 (R15 AREA) and PAR-25-298 (R15 REAP), each expiring 01-08-2028, with PAR-27-078 (R15 REAP, expires 10-26-2027), PA-25-080 (R13, expires 09-08-2027) and PA-26-002 (PF5, expires 05-08-2029), and carries no statement that any is paused or withdrawn [1](#cite:1). The PA-25-301 notice lists October 05, 2026 as a due date for new R01 applications, followed by February 05, 2027, and PA-25-304 and PA-25-302 list October 16, 2026 [4](#cite:4) [5](#cite:5) [6](#cite:6).

who_may_apply.investigator: Eligibility is set in each parent notice; the parent R01 accepts any individual with the skills, knowledge and resources to carry out the research [4](#cite:4).
who_may_apply.limits: NIH accepts six new, [renewal](#term:renewal), [resubmission](#term:resubmission) or revision applications per [principal investigator](#term:principal-investigator) per calendar year, across all activity codes except T codes and R13 [12](#cite:12).

steps: The organization holds registrations in [SAM](#term:sam-gov) (with a [Unique Entity Identifier](#term:uei)), [Grants.gov](#term:grants-gov) and [eRA Commons](#term:era-commons) before it applies [4](#cite:4) [117](#cite:117).
The applicant picks the parent notice for the activity code and checks which institutes take part, because not every institute joins every parent announcement [43](#cite:43) [1](#cite:1).
The applicant may contact a programme official, found through the Matchmaker tool or Section VII of the notice, to ask whether the plan fits the institute [120](#cite:120) [92](#cite:92).
The application goes to Grants.gov by 5 p.m. local time on the due date [121](#cite:121) [2](#cite:2).

cycle.pattern: Parent announcements typically use the standard due dates, with three cycles a year, and are usually reissued when they expire [1](#cite:1) [2](#cite:2).

distinctive: NIH describes these notices as the way to submit investigator-initiated applications on a wide range of topics [1](#cite:1).

A request for information proposes to stop reporting final overall [impact scores](#term:impact-score) and [percentiles](#term:percentile) and to report three categories instead; comments close October 13, 2026 [14](#cite:14).

name: NIH Research Project Grant (R01)
what: The [R01](#term:r01) supports a discrete, specified research project carried out by the named investigator or investigators in their area of competence [3](#cite:3). NIH calls it its most commonly used grant programme for independent research projects [42](#cite:42). The budget is not capped and the project may run up to five years [4](#cite:4). An R01 can be renewed by competing for a further [project period](#term:budget-period) [42](#cite:42).
status_note: PA-25-301 is listed as Open on [Grants.gov](#term:grants-gov), posted December 18, 2024 and closing January 7, 2028 [112](#cite:112). The notice gives an expiration date of January 08, 2028 and lists October 05, 2026, February 05, 2027, June 05, 2027 and October 05, 2027 as the remaining due dates for new applications [4](#cite:4).

who_may_apply.investigator: Any individual with the skills, knowledge and resources to carry out the research may be the programme director/[principal investigator](#term:principal-investigator) (PD/PI); NIH's orientation page says a PD/PI need not be a U.S. citizen for most programmes [4](#cite:4) [117](#cite:117).
who_may_apply.limits: An organization may submit more than one application if each is scientifically distinct; each PD/PI is limited to six applications of all kinds per calendar year [4](#cite:4) [12](#cite:12).

steps: The organization registers in [SAM](#term:sam-gov), Grants.gov and [eRA Commons](#term:era-commons), and each PD/PI links an [ORCID iD](#term:orcid) to the eRA Commons account [4](#cite:4) [31](#cite:31).

The budget uses the modular format when [direct costs](#term:direct-costs) are $250,000 a year or less and a detailed budget above that; a foreign applicant always uses the detailed budget [36](#cite:36).
No institute agreement is needed before requesting $500,000 or more in direct costs in a year, a step NIH removed on December 3, 2025 [37](#cite:37).
The application is submitted through Grants.gov by 5 p.m. local time on the due date [121](#cite:121).

After [study section](#term:study-section) and council, the [institute or center](#term:institute-or-center) director decides; a just-in-time request for more information is not an award decision [15](#cite:15) [122](#cite:122).

cycle.pattern: Standard due dates: new applications February 5, June 5 and October 5; [renewals](#term:renewal), [resubmissions](#term:resubmission) and revisions March 5, July 5 and November 5 [2](#cite:2).

Parent R01, clinical trial required; posted December 18, 2024 [144](#cite:144).

awards.amount: not limited; the budget reflects the actual needs of the project

indirect_costs: [F&A costs](#term:indirect-costs) are paid on top of direct costs at the organization's [negotiated rate](#term:nicra); a foreign organization receives 8 percent of [modified total direct costs](#term:mtdc) [64](#cite:64) [36](#cite:36).
cost_sharing: Not required [4](#cite:4).
review: A study section scores Factor 1 (Importance of the Research) and Factor 2 (Rigor and Feasibility) from 1 to 9 and rates Factor 3 (Expertise and Resources) as sufficient or insufficient; an institute [advisory council](#term:advisory-council) gives the second level of review [4](#cite:4) [41](#cite:41) [38](#cite:38).

R01-equivalent success rate: 7,000 awards from 37,478 applications [81](#cite:81).

A different measure: applicant funding rate for [early stage investigators](#term:early-stage-investigator) on new R01-equivalent applications (unique awardees over unique applicants); new non-ESI 10.0%, at-risk 16.9%, established 19.6% [82](#cite:82).

distinctive: NIH's own phrase is 'NIH's most commonly used grant program for independent research projects'; applications in which every PD/PI is an early stage investigator are prioritised for funding [42](#cite:42) [138](#cite:138).

name: NIH Exploratory/Developmental Research Grant (R21)
what: The [R21](#term:r21-r03) encourages the development of new research activities; support is restricted in amount and in time [3](#cite:3). A project runs up to two years with combined [direct costs](#term:direct-costs) of at most $275,000 [5](#cite:5). Preliminary data are not required [43](#cite:43). An R21 cannot be renewed [43](#cite:43).
status_note: PA-25-304 carries an expiration date of January 08, 2028 and lists October 16, 2026 as the next due date for new applications, followed by February 16, 2027, June 16, 2027 and October 16, 2027 [5](#cite:5). The [parent announcements](#term:parent-announcement) page lists PA-25-304 and PA-25-306, both expiring 01-08-2028 [1](#cite:1).

who_may_apply.limits: An organization may submit more than one application if each is scientifically distinct; the six-per-year limit per [PD/PI](#term:principal-investigator) applies [5](#cite:5) [12](#cite:12).

steps: The applicant checks that the target institute takes part in the parent R21, because not all do [43](#cite:43).
The application is submitted through [Grants.gov](#term:grants-gov) on a standard due date [2](#cite:2) [121](#cite:121).

cycle.pattern: Standard due dates: new applications February 16, June 16 and October 16; [renewals](#term:renewal), [resubmissions](#term:resubmission) and revisions March 16, July 16 and November 16 [2](#cite:2).

current_notices.note: Parent R21, clinical trial not allowed; posted December 18, 2024; NCI, NHLBI, NINDS and NCATS joined by later notices in 2025 and 2026 [5](#cite:5).
Parent R21, clinical trial required; posted December 18, 2024; not read in this sweep [1](#cite:1).

direct costs in any single year

indirect_costs: [F&A costs](#term:indirect-costs) are paid at the organization's [negotiated rate](#term:nicra) [64](#cite:64).
cost_sharing: Not required [5](#cite:5).
review: The simplified three-factor framework applies to R21 applications; the research strategy is limited to 6 pages [41](#cite:41) [43](#cite:43).

success.note: Applicant [funding rate](#term:success-rate) for [early stage investigators](#term:early-stage-investigator) on new R21 applications, not a success rate; new non-ESI 8.4%, at-risk 17.5%, established 20.1% [82](#cite:82).
Applicant funding rate for early stage investigators on new R21 applications; new non-ESI 13.3%, at-risk 22.3%, established 26.4% [82](#cite:82).

distinctive: [NIH](#term:nih) frames the R21 as support for new, exploratory work that 'need not have extensive background material or preliminary information' [5](#cite:5).

name: NIH Small Research Grant (R03)
what: The [R03](#term:r21-r03) supports small research projects that can be carried out in a short time with limited resources [44](#cite:44). Budgets are limited to $50,000 in [direct costs](#term:direct-costs) a year for at most two years [6](#cite:6). [NIH](#term:nih) names pilot studies, secondary analysis of existing data, small self-contained projects and development of methods or technology as typical uses [44](#cite:44). An R03 cannot be renewed [44](#cite:44).
status_note: PA-25-302 carries an expiration date of January 8, 2028 and lists October 16, 2026 as the next due date for new applications, followed by February 16, 2027, June 16, 2027 and October 16, 2027 [6](#cite:6). The standard due dates page gives February 16, June 16 and October 16 for new R03 applications [2](#cite:2).

who_may_apply.investigator: NIH's R03 page says doctoral students may not use the R03 to support a thesis or dissertation [44](#cite:44).
who_may_apply.limits: The six-per-year limit per [PD/PI](#term:principal-investigator) applies [12](#cite:12).

steps: The applicant checks which institutes take part in the parent R03 [6](#cite:6) [44](#cite:44).
The application is submitted through [Grants.gov](#term:grants-gov) on a standard due date [2](#cite:2) [121](#cite:121).

cycle.pattern: Standard due dates: new applications February 16, June 16 and October 16; [resubmissions](#term:resubmission) and revisions March 16, July 16 and November 16 [2](#cite:2).

current_notices.note: Parent R03, clinical trial not allowed; posted December 18, 2024; NCI joined February 10, 2026 and NCATS July 16, 2026 [6](#cite:6).

indirect_costs: [F&A costs](#term:indirect-costs) are paid at the organization's [negotiated rate](#term:nicra) [64](#cite:64).
cost_sharing: Not required [6](#cite:6).
review: The simplified three-factor framework applies to R03 applications; the research strategy is limited to 6 pages [41](#cite:41) [44](#cite:44).
distinctive: NIH describes the R03 as support 'specifically limited in time and amount' for preliminary, short-term projects [3](#cite:3).

name: NIH Academic Research Enhancement Award for Undergraduate-Focused Institutions (R15 AREA)
what: The [R15](#term:r15) supports small-scale research projects at educational institutions that train many of the nation's research scientists but have not been major recipients of [NIH](#term:nih) support [3](#cite:3). The AREA version is for undergraduate-focused institutions [7](#cite:7). NIH states three goals: support meritorious research, expose students to research, and strengthen the institution's research environment [45](#cite:45). An award is up to $375,000 in [direct costs](#term:direct-costs) for a project of up to three years [7](#cite:7).
status_note: PAR-25-134 carries an expiration date of January 8, 2028 and lists October 25, 2026 as the next application due date, followed by February 25, 2027, June 25, 2027 and October 25, 2027 [7](#cite:7). The [parent announcements](#term:parent-announcement) page lists PAR-25-134 and PAR-25-148 (clinical trial required), both expiring 01-08-2028 [1](#cite:1).

who_may_apply.investigator: The [PD/PI](#term:principal-investigator) holds a primary appointment at a non-health-professional school or college of the applicant institution, is not PD/PI of an active NIH research [grant](#term:grant) at the time of award, and may hold only one R15 at a time [7](#cite:7).
who_may_apply.limits: One R15 per PD/PI at a time; the six-per-year application limit per PD/PI also applies [7](#cite:7) [12](#cite:12).

steps: The institution confirms it meets the AREA test; a signed letter from the provost or similar official verifying eligibility goes in the application [45](#cite:45).
A budget of $250,000 or less in direct costs uses the modular format; $250,001 to $375,000 uses the R&R budget form [45](#cite:45).
The application is submitted through [Grants.gov](#term:grants-gov) on an R15 due date [2](#cite:2) [121](#cite:121).

cycle.pattern: Standard due dates for all R15 application types: February 25, June 25 and October 25 [2](#cite:2).

current_notices.note: AREA, clinical trial not allowed; posted November 26, 2024; the notice carries a header line dated March 31, 2025 saying it was updated to align with agency priorities [7](#cite:7).
AREA, clinical trial required; posted November 21, 2024; not read in this sweep [1](#cite:1).

awards.label: direct costs for the entire project period, excluding consortium F&A

indirect_costs: [F&A costs](#term:indirect-costs) are paid at the institution's [negotiated rate](#term:nicra); the $375,000 limit counts direct costs only [7](#cite:7) [64](#cite:64).
cost_sharing: Not required [7](#cite:7).
review: The three simplified factors are used, with added questions on the effect on the institution's research environment, the plan to involve undergraduates, and the investigator's record of supervising students [7](#cite:7).
distinctive: NIH frames the R15 around students: the application proposes a research team that includes undergraduate or graduate students [45](#cite:45).

name: NIH Research Enhancement Award Program for Health Professional Schools and Graduate Schools (R15 REAP)
what: REAP is the [R15](#term:r15) for health professional schools and graduate schools that have received limited [NIH](#term:nih) support [8](#cite:8). It shares the three R15 goals of supporting meritorious research, exposing students to research and strengthening the institution's research environment [45](#cite:45). An award is up to $375,000 in [direct costs](#term:direct-costs) for a project of up to three years [8](#cite:8).
status_note: PAR-25-298 carries an expiration date of January 08, 2028 and lists October 25, 2026 as the next due date for new, [renewal](#term:renewal) and [resubmission](#term:resubmission) applications, followed by February 25, 2027, June 25, 2027 and October 25, 2027 [8](#cite:8). The [parent announcements](#term:parent-announcement) page lists PAR-25-298 (expires 01-08-2028) and PAR-27-078, clinical trial required (released 05-29-2026, expires 10-26-2027) [1](#cite:1).

who_may_apply.investigator: The [PD/PI](#term:principal-investigator) holds a primary appointment at an R15-eligible organization, is not PD/PI of an active NIH research [grant](#term:grant), and may hold only one R15 at a time [45](#cite:45).
who_may_apply.limits: One R15 per PD/PI at a time; the six-per-year application limit per PD/PI also applies [45](#cite:45) [12](#cite:12).

steps: The institution confirms that all its components together stayed at or under the NIH support threshold, and a signed letter from the provost or similar official verifies eligibility [8](#cite:8) [45](#cite:45).
The application is submitted through [Grants.gov](#term:grants-gov) on an R15 due date [2](#cite:2) [121](#cite:121).

cycle.pattern: Standard due dates for all R15 application types: February 25, June 25 and October 25 [2](#cite:2).

REAP, clinical trial required; posted May 29, 2026; not read in this sweep [1](#cite:1).

indirect_costs: [F&A costs](#term:indirect-costs) are paid at the institution's [negotiated rate](#term:nicra); the $375,000 limit counts direct costs only [8](#cite:8) [64](#cite:64).
cost_sharing: Not required [8](#cite:8).
review: The simplified three-factor framework applies to R15 applications [41](#cite:41).
distinctive: REAP defines its schools by the degrees they grant, from BSN and MD to MPH, and graduate schools by M.A., M.S. and Ph.D. degrees [8](#cite:8).

name: NIH Planning Grant (R34)
what: The R34 supports the early development of a clinical trial or research project: forming the team, building data-management and oversight tools, and writing the protocol, recruitment strategy and procedure manuals [3](#cite:3). [NIH](#term:nih) has no parent R34; each institute that uses the code issues its own notice [1](#cite:1) [109](#cite:109). NIH's R34 page lists 18 participating [institutes and centers](#term:institute-or-center) [46](#cite:46).
status_note: R34 notices are institute-specific; PAR-25-032 (NHLBI Clinical Trial Pilot Studies) is listed as Open on [Grants.gov](#term:grants-gov), posted December 18, 2024 and closing January 7, 2027 [114](#cite:114). The Grants.gov search for posted R34 planning [grants](#term:grant) returns five Open notices, among them PAR-25-358 (closes Jan 7, 2028), PAR-25-104 (closes Oct 25, 2027) and PAR-25-159 (closes Jan 7, 2027) [109](#cite:109).

who_may_apply.limits: The six-per-year application limit per [PD/PI](#term:principal-investigator) applies [12](#cite:12).

steps: The applicant finds an institute's own R34 notice on Grants.gov, since there is no parent R34 [109](#cite:109) [1](#cite:1).
The application is submitted through Grants.gov on the dates in that notice [121](#cite:121).

cycle.pattern: New R34 applications follow the standard dates February 16, June 16 and October 16 unless the notice says otherwise [2](#cite:2).

NEI Clinical Research Study Planning Grant Program (R34); posted January 10, 2025 [109](#cite:109).

Prevention and Intervention Approaches for Fetal Alcohol Spectrum Disorders (R34); posted November 25, 2024 [109](#cite:109).

review: The simplified three-factor framework applies to R34 applications [41](#cite:41).
distinctive: NHLBI describes its R34 as pilot work 'necessary and sufficient to inform the planning of a Phase II-IV clinical trial' [114](#cite:114).

name: NIH Phased Exploratory/Developmental Award (R61/R33)
what: The R61/R33 is a two-phase award. The R61 pays for the first, exploratory phase, and [NIH](#term:nih) uses it in place of the [R21](#term:r21-r03) when a larger budget or longer period is needed to show a project is feasible [3](#cite:3) [50](#cite:50). The R33 is the second phase [3](#cite:3). Moving from the first phase to the second depends on meeting milestones set in the application [115](#cite:115). The code is offered only through institute notices, of which 25 were open on the sweep date [108](#cite:108).
status_note: R61/R33 notices are institute-specific; the [Grants.gov](#term:grants-gov) search for posted R61/R33 opportunities returns 25 Open notices, among them PAR-27-011 (posted Mar 18, 2026, closes Nov 2, 2028), PAR-28-072 (posted Sep 25, 2026, closes Nov 16, 2029) and PAR-25-059 (posted Oct 22, 2024, closes Oct 20, 2027) [108](#cite:108).

who_may_apply.investigator: Set in each notice; NHLBI's funding policy says [early stage investigator](#term:early-stage-investigator) status does not apply to the second phase of phased awards [70](#cite:70).
who_may_apply.limits: The six-per-year application limit per [PD/PI](#term:principal-investigator) applies [12](#cite:12).

steps: The applicant finds an institute notice that uses the R61/R33 code on Grants.gov [108](#cite:108).
The application states milestones for the first phase; the second phase is funded only if they are met [115](#cite:115).

cycle.pattern: Dates are set in each notice; the standard dates for new R21/R33-type applications are February 16, June 16 and October 16 [2](#cite:2) [115](#cite:115).

review: The simplified three-factor framework covers R61, R33 and R61/R33 applications; in the NHLBI example, programme staff run an administrative review about 9 months into the R61 phase to check milestones [41](#cite:41) [115](#cite:115).

name: NIH Investigator-Focused Award (R35), including the NIGMS Maximizing Investigators' Research Award (MIRA)
what: The R35 supports an investigator's whole research programme within one institute's mission rather than a single project, and lets the investigator change direction inside that mission [3](#cite:3) [47](#cite:47). [NIH](#term:nih)'s R35 page shows two users, NHLBI and NIGMS [47](#cite:47). The NIGMS version is the Maximizing Investigators' Research Award (MIRA), with one notice for established and [new investigators](#term:early-stage-investigator) and one for early stage investigators [72](#cite:72). A MIRA runs five years [72](#cite:72).
status_note: Both NIGMS MIRA notices are listed as Open on [Grants.gov](#term:grants-gov): PAR-26-121 (established and new investigators), closing May 26, 2028, and PAR-27-032 (early stage investigators), posted May 12, 2026 and closing February 6, 2029 [2513](#cite:2513) [2514](#cite:2514). The PAR-26-121 announcement lists January 27, 2027 as its next application due date, followed by May 27, 2027, January 27, 2028 and May 26, 2028 [73](#cite:73).

who_may_apply.investigator: PAR-26-121 is open to investigators holding at least one NIGMS single-PI R01-equivalent award, current MIRA holders renewing, and new investigators who are not early stage investigators; PAR-27-032 is for early stage investigators [73](#cite:73) [74](#cite:74).
who_may_apply.limits: Single [PD/PI](#term:principal-investigator) only, one application per investigator; the fetched text gives a minimum effort of 45% of total research effort in PAR-26-121 and at least 51% in PAR-27-032 [73](#cite:73) [74](#cite:74).

steps: The investigator checks eligibility against the NIGMS decision tree and the notice [72](#cite:72).
The application is submitted through Grants.gov on a MIRA due date [73](#cite:73) [74](#cite:74).
owner: National Institutes of Health (HHS); MIRA is run by the National Institute of General Medical Sciences

cycle.pattern: MIRA uses its own dates, not the standard ones: January 27 and May 27 for PAR-26-121, and early October and early February for PAR-27-032 [73](#cite:73) [74](#cite:74).

current_notices.note: MIRA for established and new investigators; due January 27, 2027; May 27, 2027; January 27, 2028; May 26, 2028 [73](#cite:73).
MIRA for early stage investigators; posted May 12, 2026; due October 2, 2026; February 3, 2027; October 4, 2027; February 3, 2028; October 3, 2028; February 6, 2029 [74](#cite:74).

awards.label: MIRA, established and new investigators, direct costs per year (maximum)
MIRA, early stage investigators, direct costs per year

indirect_costs: [F&A costs](#term:indirect-costs) are paid at the organization's [negotiated rate](#term:nicra) [64](#cite:64).
cost_sharing: Not required [73](#cite:73) [74](#cite:74).
review: The R35 is not on NIH's list of codes under the simplified framework; PAR-26-121 as fetched lists Significance, Investigator(s), Innovation, Approach and Environment [41](#cite:41) [73](#cite:73).
distinctive: NIGMS says MIRA aims to 'increase the stability of funding for NIGMS-supported investigators' and to 'reduce the time spent by researchers writing and reviewing [grant](#term:grant) applications'; NIGMS generally funds MIRA ahead of [R01](#term:r01) awards [73](#cite:73) [71](#cite:71).

pending_changes.text: [NIH](#term:nih)'s Deputy Director for Extramural Research wrote that NIH is expanding the number of broad funding opportunities, naming P01 programme projects as an example [90](#cite:90).

name: NIH Research Program Project Grant (P01)
what: The P01 supports a broadly based, multidisciplinary and often long-term research programme with one major objective or theme [3](#cite:3). It funds several related projects, each usually led by an established investigator, and shared resources [48](#cite:48). NIH has no parent P01; institutes issue their own notices, and NIH's P01 page shows NHLBI and NIAID as users [1](#cite:1) [48](#cite:48). One open P01 notice was found on [Grants.gov](#term:grants-gov) on the sweep date, from NIAID [110](#cite:110).
status_note: The Grants.gov search for posted P01 opportunities returns one notice, PAR-27-082 (NIAID Investigator Initiated Program Project Applications), listed as Open, posted May 7, 2026 and closing May 25, 2029 [110](#cite:110). The announcement lists January 25, 2027 as the next application due date after September 25, 2026 and an expiration date of May 26, 2029 [113](#cite:113).

who_may_apply.investigator: In the NIAID notice any qualified individual may lead; multiple PD/[PIs](#term:principal-investigator) are allowed only for the overall programme leader, not for project or core leaders [113](#cite:113).
who_may_apply.limits: Foreign organizations may not apply for programme project [grants](#term:grant) [107](#cite:107) [113](#cite:113).

steps: NIAID strongly encourages consultation with its staff at least 15 weeks before the due date [113](#cite:113).
The application has at least two related research projects and an administrative core; scientific cores are optional [113](#cite:113).
A collaboration that would pay a foreign organization goes to a notice designated for funded international collaborations instead [113](#cite:113).

cycle.pattern: P series applications of all types follow the standard dates January 25, May 25 and September 25 [2](#cite:2).

current_notices.note: NIAID Investigator Initiated Program Project Applications (P01, clinical trial not allowed); posted May 07, 2026; first due date September 25, 2026, next January 25, 2027 [113](#cite:113).

awards.label: NIAID P01 (PAR-27-082)
awards.amount: not limited; the budget reflects the actual needs of the project

indirect_costs: [F&A costs](#term:indirect-costs) are paid at the organization's [negotiated rate](#term:nicra) [64](#cite:64).
cost_sharing: Not required in the NIAID notice [113](#cite:113).
review: The NIAID notice as fetched reviews the overall programme and each project on Significance, Investigator(s), Innovation, Approach and Environment, with separate criteria for the administrative and scientific cores [113](#cite:113).
distinctive: NIAID asks for 'at least two related, synergistic Research Projects that share a common central theme' [113](#cite:113).

name: NIH Research Project Cooperative Agreement (U01)
what: The [U01](#term:u01) funds the same kind of discrete research project as the [R01](#term:r01), under a [cooperative agreement](#term:cooperative-agreement) instead of a [grant](#term:grant) [49](#cite:49) [3](#cite:3). A cooperative agreement is [financial assistance](#term:financial-assistance) in which the federal agency is substantially involved in carrying out the work [106](#cite:106). After award, [NIH](#term:nih) scientific or programme staff assist, guide, coordinate or take part in project activities [116](#cite:116). There is no parent U01; 33 programme-specific U01 notices were open on [Grants.gov](#term:grants-gov) on the sweep date [111](#cite:111).
status_note: U01 notices are institute-specific; the Grants.gov search for posted U01 clinical-trial opportunities returns 33 results, with PAR-27-064 (posted Jun 16, 2026, closes Jul 5, 2029), PAR-25-297 (closes Nov 5, 2027) and PAR-24-325 (closes Sep 7, 2027) each shown as Open [111](#cite:111). The standard due dates page gives February 5, June 5 and October 5 for new U01 applications where a notice uses standard dates [2](#cite:2).

who_may_apply.investigator: Set in each notice; NIH's U01 page says [early stage investigators](#term:early-stage-investigator) receive special consideration when every [PD/PI](#term:principal-investigator) has that status [49](#cite:49).
who_may_apply.limits: The six-per-year application limit per PD/PI applies [12](#cite:12).

steps: The applicant finds a programme-specific U01 notice on Grants.gov [111](#cite:111).

The notice's cooperative agreement terms name the NIH staff roles; in the NIAID example a Project Scientist monitors the trial and a [Program Official](#term:program-officer) provides normal stewardship [116](#cite:116).
Disagreements under the NIAID example go to a three-member panel: one member named by the recipient, one by NIH, and an outside expert chosen by those two [116](#cite:116).

cycle.pattern: Where a notice uses standard dates, new U01 applications are due February 5, June 5 and October 5 and [renewals](#term:renewal), [resubmissions](#term:resubmission) and revisions March 5, July 5 and November 5 [2](#cite:2).

current_notices.note: NIAID Clinical Trial Implementation Cooperative Agreement (U01, clinical trial required); posted June 16, 2026; first due dates October 05, 2026 (new) and November 05, 2026 (renewal, resubmission) [116](#cite:116).
Alzheimer's Drug-Development Program (U01); posted December 4, 2024 [111](#cite:111).
Bioengineering Partnerships with Industry (U01); posted November 6, 2024 [111](#cite:111).

awards.label: NIAID clinical trial implementation U01 (PAR-27-064)
awards.amount: not limited; the budget reflects the actual needs of the project

indirect_costs: [F&A costs](#term:indirect-costs) are paid at the organization's [negotiated rate](#term:nicra); a foreign organization receives 8 percent of [modified total direct costs](#term:mtdc) [64](#cite:64).
review: The simplified three-factor framework covers U01 applications [41](#cite:41).
distinctive: The difference from a grant is NIH's part in the work: 'After award, NIH scientific or program staff will assist, guide, coordinate, or participate in project activities' [116](#cite:116).

name: NIH Director's Pioneer Award (DP1)
what: The Pioneer Award supports individuals with the potential to make extraordinary contributions to medical research [3](#cite:3). It is open to investigators at all career stages who pursue a new research direction [53](#cite:53). The award is $700,000 in direct costs a year for five years, requested as a single $3,500,000 figure with no detailed budget [75](#cite:75). Preliminary data and detailed experimental plans are not required [75](#cite:75).
status_note: RFA-RM-27-001 is listed as Closed on [Grants.gov](#term:grants-gov), posted June 29, 2026 with a closing date of September 9, 2026 [2515](#cite:2515). The Common Fund's Pioneer Award page states "No open funding announcements" and points to its funding opportunities page for information about future announcements, and neither it nor the High-Risk, High-Reward page gives a date for the next round or says the award has ended [2516](#cite:2516) [53](#cite:53).

who_may_apply.investigator: A single [PD/PI](#term:principal-investigator) at any career stage, committing more than 6 person-months (at least 51%) of research effort in the first three years [75](#cite:75) [53](#cite:53).
who_may_apply.limits: One application per individual as PD/PI; foreign organizations are not eligible [75](#cite:75).

steps: The applicant watches for the yearly notice on Grants.gov; the four FY 2027 notices were posted on June 26 and June 29, 2026 [75](#cite:75) [102](#cite:102) [103](#cite:103) [104](#cite:104).
The application enters $3,500,000 as total federal funds requested; no detailed budget forms are filed [75](#cite:75).
owner: NIH Common Fund, High-Risk, High-Reward Research Program

cycle.pattern: One notice a year with a single due date; the FY 2027 round closed September 9, 2026 [75](#cite:75) [53](#cite:53).

current_notices.note: Posted June 29, 2026; due September 9, 2026; expired September 10, 2026; no later notice was found in this sweep [75](#cite:75).

awards.label: direct costs per year
awards.duration: 5 years ($3,500,000 total entered by the applicant)

indirect_costs: The notice states the award in [direct costs](#term:direct-costs); [F&A costs](#term:indirect-costs) follow the organization's [negotiated rate](#term:nicra) under the [Grants](#term:grant) Policy Statement [75](#cite:75) [64](#cite:64).
cost_sharing: Not required [75](#cite:75).
review: A [scientific review group](#term:study-section) reads the applications, roughly the top half go on to discussion, selected candidates are interviewed (March-April 2027 for this round), and an [NIH](#term:nih) [advisory council](#term:advisory-council) gives the second-level review [75](#cite:75).
distinctive: The Common Fund says the programme was 'created to accelerate the pace of biomedical and behavioral breakthroughs by supporting exceptional, creative scientists with innovative ideas' [53](#cite:53).

name: NIH Director's New Innovator Award (DP2)
what: The New Innovator Award supports highly innovative research projects by [new investigators](#term:early-stage-investigator) in any area of biomedical and behavioral research [3](#cite:3). The [PD/PI](#term:principal-investigator) is an Early Stage Investigator [102](#cite:102). The award is up to $475,000 in direct costs a year for five years, $2,375,000 in all, and is multi-year funded [102](#cite:102).
status_note: RFA-RM-27-002 is listed as Closed on [Grants.gov](#term:grants-gov), posted June 26, 2026 with a closing date of August 17, 2026 [2517](#cite:2517). The Common Fund's New Innovator Award page still shows RFA-RM-27-002 with "Applications due August 17, 2026" and gives neither a date for the next round nor a statement that the award has ended [76](#cite:76).

who_may_apply.investigator: A single PD/PI who meets the Early Stage Investigator definition, commits at least three person-months (25%) of effort, and holds an independent position by September 1, 2027 for the FY 2027 round [102](#cite:102).
who_may_apply.limits: One application per individual as PD/PI; foreign organizations are not eligible [102](#cite:102).

steps: The investigator confirms Early Stage Investigator status in the [eRA Commons](#term:era-commons) profile, where [NIH](#term:nih) computes it [138](#cite:138).
The application is submitted through Grants.gov by the single due date [102](#cite:102).
owner: NIH Common Fund, High-Risk, High-Reward Research Program

cycle.pattern: One notice a year with a single due date; the FY 2027 round closed August 17, 2026 [102](#cite:102) [76](#cite:76).

current_notices.note: Posted June 26, 2026; due August 17, 2026; expired August 18, 2026 [102](#cite:102).

indirect_costs: The notice states the award in [direct costs](#term:direct-costs); [F&A costs](#term:indirect-costs) follow the organization's [negotiated rate](#term:nicra) under the [Grants](#term:grant) Policy Statement [102](#cite:102) [64](#cite:64).
cost_sharing: Not required [102](#cite:102).
review: Review has two phases, mail reviewers and then a panel discussion; the NIH Council of Councils gives the second-level review [102](#cite:102).
distinctive: The Common Fund says the award 'supports early career investigators of exceptional creativity who propose bold and highly innovative research projects' [76](#cite:76).

name: NIH Director's Early Independence Award (DP5)
what: The Early Independence Award supports the independent research project of a recent doctoral degree recipient [3](#cite:3). It lets a newly graduated scientist skip the usual postdoctoral period and start an independent research position [78](#cite:78). The award is up to $350,000 in [direct costs](#term:direct-costs) a year for up to five years [104](#cite:104). Each institution may submit only two applications [104](#cite:104).
status_note: RFA-RM-27-004 is listed as Closed on [Grants.gov](#term:grants-gov), posted June 26, 2026 with a closing date of September 10, 2026 [2518](#cite:2518). The Common Fund's Early Independence Award page states "No open funding announcements" and points to its funding opportunities page for information about future announcements, with no date for the next round and no statement that the award has ended [78](#cite:78) [53](#cite:53).

who_may_apply.investigator: For the FY 2027 round, a terminal doctoral degree or post-graduate clinical training completed between May 1, 2025 and September 30, 2027; a non-independent position at the time of application; at least 9.6 person-months (80% effort) a year [104](#cite:104).
who_may_apply.limits: Only two applications per institution, counted by [Unique Entity Identifier](#term:uei) or [NIH](#term:nih) IPF number; foreign organizations are not eligible [104](#cite:104).

steps: The institution chooses which two candidates it will put forward, because of the two-application limit [104](#cite:104).
The application is submitted through Grants.gov by the single due date [104](#cite:104).
owner: NIH Common Fund, High-Risk, High-Reward Research Program

cycle.pattern: One notice a year with a single due date; the FY 2027 round closed September 10, 2026 [104](#cite:104) [53](#cite:53).

current_notices.note: Posted June 26, 2026; due September 10, 2026; expired September 11, 2026 [104](#cite:104).

indirect_costs: The notice gives the amount as direct costs 'plus any allowed [indirect costs](#term:indirect-costs)' [104](#cite:104).
cost_sharing: Not required [104](#cite:104).
review: Three experts in the subject score and comment on each application, and an editorial panel then reviews against the same criteria [104](#cite:104).
distinctive: The Common Fund says the award lets 'promising, newly graduated scientists' bypass 'the traditional postgraduate training period to launch independent research careers' [78](#cite:78).

name: NIH Director's Transformative Research Award (R01)
what: The Transformative Research Award supports individuals or teams proposing projects that are risky and untested but could create or overturn fundamental paradigms [77](#cite:77). It uses the [R01](#term:r01) [activity code](#term:activity-code) under its own yearly notice [103](#cite:103). Budgets are not limited and the project runs up to five years [103](#cite:103). Preliminary data are not required [77](#cite:77).
status_note: RFA-RM-27-003 is listed as Closed on [Grants.gov](#term:grants-gov), posted June 29, 2026 with a closing date of September 3, 2026 [2519](#cite:2519). The Common Fund's Transformative Research Award page states "No open funding announcements" and points to its funding opportunities page for information about future announcements, with no date for the next round and no statement that the award has ended [77](#cite:77) [53](#cite:53).

who_may_apply.investigator: Any qualified individual or team at any career stage; multiple PD/[PIs](#term:principal-investigator) are permitted [103](#cite:103) [77](#cite:77).
who_may_apply.limits: An organization may submit more than one application if each is scientifically distinct; foreign organizations are not eligible [103](#cite:103).

steps: The applicant watches for the yearly notice on Grants.gov [103](#cite:103) [77](#cite:77).
The application is submitted through Grants.gov by the single due date [103](#cite:103).
owner: NIH Common Fund, High-Risk, High-Reward Research Program

cycle.pattern: One notice a year with a single due date; the FY 2027 round closed September 3, 2026 [103](#cite:103) [53](#cite:53).

current_notices.note: Posted June 29, 2026; due September 03, 2026; expired September 04, 2026 [103](#cite:103).

awards.label: direct costs
awards.amount: not limited; commensurate with the scope of the research

indirect_costs: [F&A costs](#term:indirect-costs) are paid at the organization's [negotiated rate](#term:nicra) [64](#cite:64).
cost_sharing: Not required [103](#cite:103).
review: Review has three phases: an editorial panel reads the aims, mail reviewers write critiques, and the editorial panel discusses and scores the selected applications [103](#cite:103).
distinctive: The Common Fund describes projects 'that are inherently risky and untested but have the potential to create or overturn fundamental paradigms' [77](#cite:77).

conflicts: Posted date: October 02, 2024 on the notice [52](#cite:52) vs 10-01-2024 in the parent-announcement table [1](#cite:1).
name: NIH Support for Conferences and Scientific Meetings (R13)
what: The R13 supports international, national or regional meetings, conferences and workshops that the recipient sponsors and directs [3](#cite:3). Only organizations may apply; an individual cannot receive a conference [grant](#term:grant) [52](#cite:52). Most institutes accept applications for up to five years of support when a series of annual or biannual conferences is proposed [51](#cite:51). [F&A](#term:indirect-costs) (indirect) costs are not allowed [51](#cite:51).
status_note: PA-25-080 carries an expiration date of September 08, 2027 and lists December 12, 2026 as the next due date for new and [renewal](#term:renewal) applications, followed by April 12, 2027 and August 12, 2027 [52](#cite:52). The standard due dates page gives April 12, August 12 and December 12 for R13 and U13 applications [2](#cite:2).

who_may_apply.investigator: The applicant is an organization, such as a domestic institution or an established scientific or professional society; an individual is not eligible [51](#cite:51) [52](#cite:52).
who_may_apply.limits: Foreign organizations are not eligible; R13 applications do not count toward the six-per-year limit per [PD/PI](#term:principal-investigator) [52](#cite:52) [12](#cite:12).

steps: No advance permission from an institute is needed for due dates on or after April 12, 2026 [52](#cite:52) [97](#cite:97).
An applicant may state which institute it prefers on the PHS Assignment Request Form [97](#cite:97).
The budget leaves out the costs the notice bars, which include meals, equipment, honoraria, dues and indirect costs [52](#cite:52).

cycle.pattern: Standard due dates for R13 and U13: April 12, August 12 and December 12 [2](#cite:2).

current_notices.note: Parent R13; remaining due dates December 12, 2026; April 12, 2027; August 12, 2027 [52](#cite:52).

awards.label: budget
awards.amount: not limited; the budget reflects the actual needs of the project
awards.duration: up to 5 years for a conference series at most institutes

indirect_costs: Not allowed; conference grants receive no F&A costs [51](#cite:51) [64](#cite:64).
cost_sharing: Not required [52](#cite:52).
review: The [parent notice](#term:parent-announcement) as fetched lists Significance, Investigator(s), Innovation, Approach and Environment and an [overall impact score](#term:impact-score) [52](#cite:52).
distinctive: [NIH](#term:nih)'s wording is support for 'recipient sponsored and directed international, national or regional meetings, conferences and workshops' [3](#cite:3).

name: NIH Collaborative International Research Project (PF5, with linked RF2 awards)
what: The PF5 is the structure [NIH](#term:nih) put in place of foreign [subawards](#term:subaward) [86](#cite:86). A domestic organization submits one multi-component application; after review each foreign collaborator's part is split off and issued as its own linked award, the RF2, with its own [grant](#term:grant) number [23](#cite:23) [86](#cite:86). NIH says the parent PF5 is for U.S.-led, investigator-initiated projects that formerly would have been proposed with a subaward to a foreign organization [87](#cite:87). Cooperative-agreement versions use the codes UF5 and UL2 [86](#cite:86).
status_note: PA-26-002 is listed as Open on [Grants.gov](#term:grants-gov), posted January 20, 2026 and closing May 7, 2029 [2520](#cite:2520). The announcement lists January 25, 2027 as the next application due date after September 25, 2026 and an expiration date of May 08, 2029 [23](#cite:23).

who_may_apply.investigator: At least one [PD/PI](#term:principal-investigator) comes from the domestic primary organization and one from each International Project [86](#cite:86).
who_may_apply.limits: A non-U.S. entity may not be the prime applicant; each International Project corresponds to a single foreign organization [23](#cite:23).

steps: The application has an Overall component, a Research Project component, and one International Project component for each foreign collaborator [86](#cite:86).
Each foreign organization supplies a letter saying it will fill the role of [recipient organization](#term:applicant-organization) [141](#cite:141).
After [merit review](#term:merit-review) NIH separates each International Project into an RF2 award made directly to the foreign organization [23](#cite:23) [86](#cite:86).

cycle.pattern: Due dates are May 25, September 25 and January 25 each year, from May 25, 2026 to January 25, 2029 [23](#cite:23).

current_notices.note: Parent PF5, clinical trial optional; posted January 20, 2026; next due date January 25, 2027 [23](#cite:23) [1](#cite:1).

awards.label: budget
awards.amount: not limited; the budget reflects the actual needs of the project
awards.duration: up to 5 years, or 7 years for clinical trials, as the fetched notice reads

indirect_costs: A foreign organization receives [F&A](#term:indirect-costs) at 8 percent of [modified total direct costs](#term:mtdc); the domestic organization uses its [negotiated rate](#term:nicra) [64](#cite:64).
review: The fetched notice lists Significance, Investigator(s), Innovation, Approach and Environment [23](#cite:23).
distinctive: NIH says the structure 'establishes direct, legal relationships between NIH and each international collaborator' [87](#cite:87).

pending_changes.text: [NSF](#term:nsf) has proposed to replace the [PAPPG](#term:pappg) with a Guidance on [Financial Assistance](#term:financial-assistance); comments closed August 24, 2026 and NSF's stated goal is to issue it for use in early to mid FY2027 [152](#cite:152) [151](#cite:151).

conflicts: De minimis indirect-cost rate: 10% of MTDC in PAPPG 24-1 as printed [257](#cite:257) vs up to 15% of MTDC on NSF's indirect-costs page [163](#cite:163).
name: NSF research proposal (standard proposal under the PAPPG)
what: The research proposal is NSF's ordinary route to a research [grant](#term:grant): an organisation submits a full proposal to a programme description, programme announcement or [solicitation](#term:program-solicitation), and NSF funds it as a grant if it is recommended after [merit review](#term:merit-review) [156](#cite:156) [157](#cite:157). [Research.gov](#term:research-gov) lists Research first among the proposal types it supports [252](#cite:252).
status_note: The research proposal is a proposal type sent to a funding opportunity, not a competition of its own; NSF's news item of August 17, 2026 lists 12 foundational-research [notices of funding opportunity](#term:nofo), and one of them, NSF 26-517 (BIO Core), states "Proposals Accepted Anytime" [192](#cite:192) [185](#cite:185). The Preparing Your Proposal page still points to Chapter II of PAPPG 24-1 and carries no notice of a new guide or of a pause in accepting proposals [159](#cite:159).

who_may_apply.investigator: NSF invites proposals from all qualified scientists, engineers and educators through an eligible organisation; unaffiliated individuals are not eligible for direct funding [158](#cite:158) [156](#cite:156). A person who is a current party to a malign foreign talent recruitment program may not serve as senior/key personnel [156](#cite:156).
who_may_apply.limits: No general limit on the number of proposals was found in the PAPPG chapters read; limits are set by individual solicitations, for example two proposals per person in twelve months in CISE Future CoRe and one per fiscal year in MPS Materials [189](#cite:189) [215](#cite:215).
who_may_apply.eligibility_note: The proposer categories of PAPPG Chapter I.E apply, which include non-profit non-academic organisations located in the U.S. [156](#cite:156).

steps: The organisation obtains a [UEI](#term:uei) and an active [SAM registration](#term:sam-gov); NSF recommends doing so at least 90 days before submission [161](#cite:161).

The investigator finds a funding opportunity through the NSF Funding Search or a [directorate](#term:nsf-directorate) page and contacts a [programme officer](#term:program-officer) listed on it [155](#cite:155) [158](#cite:158).

The proposal is prepared to PAPPG Chapter II: a one-page Project Summary, a Project Description of no more than 15 pages, references, senior/key personnel documents, budget and justification, facilities, and a [data management and sharing plan](#term:data-management-plan) [159](#cite:159) [257](#cite:257).
Biographical sketches and [current and pending (other) support](#term:other-support) are prepared in [SciENcv](#term:sciencv) [248](#cite:248).
The organisation's authorised representative submits through Research.gov or [Grants.gov](#term:grants-gov) [161](#cite:161).
NSF aims to give a decision within six months and releases the reviews to the [PI](#term:principal-investigator) with reviewer identities removed [160](#cite:160) [157](#cite:157).
A declined proposal may be resubmitted only after substantial revision; reconsideration may be requested within 90 days [258](#cite:258).

cycle.pattern: Set by each funding opportunity: a deadline date, a target date, a submission window, or acceptance at any time [156](#cite:156). Proposals must be received by 5 p.m. submitting organisation's local time on a deadline date [156](#cite:156). Twelve foundational-research notices posted in August 2026 mostly accept proposals at any time [192](#cite:192) [185](#cite:185).

awards.label: award size
awards.amount: set by the funding opportunity; no general ceiling found
awards.duration: up to five years (60 months) unless a solicitation specifies otherwise

awards.label: research grants, average annualized award (FY 2027 budget request table)
research grants, median annualized award (FY 2027 budget request table)

indirect_costs: [Indirect costs](#term:indirect-costs) are budgeted at the organisation's federally [negotiated rate](#term:nicra) unless a solicitation says otherwise [257](#cite:257). The [15 percent cap](#term:indirect-rate-cap) NSF announced in May 2025 was [vacated](#term:vacatur) by a court and is not in effect [237](#cite:237) [238](#cite:238). The PAPPG as printed in 2024 gives a [de minimis rate](#term:de-minimis-rate) of 10 percent of [modified total direct costs](#term:mtdc) for organisations with no negotiated rate; NSF's indirect-cost page gives up to 15 percent [257](#cite:257) [163](#cite:163).
cost_sharing: Voluntary committed [cost sharing](#term:cost-sharing) is prohibited [257](#cite:257). NSF's cost-sharing page names I-Corps, Engineering Research Centers and [EPSCoR](#term:epscor) among the few programmes that require it [164](#cite:164).
review: Proposals are judged on the two National Science Board criteria, [Intellectual Merit and Broader Impacts](#term:intellectual-merit) [157](#cite:157). A programme officer checks compliance, obtains reviews from ad hoc reviewers, a panel or both, and recommends award or decline; the PAPPG places programmatic approval at division or office level, followed by a business review in the Division of Grants and Agreements [160](#cite:160) [157](#cite:157). Since December 8, 2025 a full proposal must be reviewed by at least two reviewers, who may be NSF staff [149](#cite:149).
distinctive: NSF describes itself as inviting proposals from all qualified scientists, engineers and educators, and the August 2026 notices say proposals need not promise a near-term product, deployment or commercial outcome [158](#cite:158) [200](#cite:200).

all competitive awards, FY 2025 plan column: 38,700 proposals, 7,400 awards

budget_rules: Salary requested for each senior/key person is limited to two months of regular salary in any one year [257](#cite:257).

pending_changes.text: [NSF](#term:nsf) has proposed to replace the [PAPPG](#term:pappg) with a Guidance on [Financial Assistance](#term:financial-assistance); comments closed August 24, 2026 and NSF's stated goal is to issue it for use in early to mid FY2027 [152](#cite:152) [151](#cite:151).

conflicts: RAPID ceiling: $300,000 in Supplement 1 [149] vs $200,000 in a third-party guide that says it includes Supplements 1 and 2 [264](#cite:264).
name: Rapid Response Research (RAPID)
what: RAPID is a proposal type defined in PAPPG Chapter II.F for time-sensitive work [257](#cite:257) [212](#cite:212). Supplement 1 to the PAPPG sets the request ceiling at $300,000 for up to one year [149](#cite:149).
status_note: RAPID is a proposal type with no notice of its own; NSF 26-517 (BIO Core) states that [RAPID proposals](#term:eager-rapid) may be submitted at any time once a [concept outline](#term:concept-outline) has been submitted and NSF BIO has approved submission [185](#cite:185). The ENG proposal guidance states that RAPID proposals can be submitted at any time after a concept outline has gone to the cognizant programme director [166](#cite:166).

who_may_apply.investigator: Same organisations and investigators as any NSF proposal [156](#cite:156).
who_may_apply.limits: MPS Chemistry exempts RAPID proposals from its two-proposals-per-year limit [213](#cite:213). No general limit was found on a page read in this sweep [257](#cite:257).
who_may_apply.eligibility_note: The proposer categories of PAPPG Chapter I.E apply, which include non-profit non-academic organisations located in the U.S. [156](#cite:156).

steps: The [PI](#term:principal-investigator) sends a concept outline to the [programme officer](#term:program-officer) by email or through ProSPCT; outlines are generally limited to two pages or 6000 characters [156](#cite:156).
In BIO, approval from the [directorate](#term:nsf-directorate) is required before the full proposal is submitted [185](#cite:185).
The proposal is prepared in [Research.gov](#term:research-gov) as proposal type RAPID [252](#cite:252).
A RAPID award can be renewed only through a [renewal](#term:renewal) proposal that goes through full external [merit review](#term:merit-review) [252](#cite:252).

cycle.pattern: May be submitted at any time, after a concept outline has gone to the programme officer [166](#cite:166) [185](#cite:185).

awards.label: request ceiling, including indirect costs (from December 8, 2025)

indirect_costs: [Indirect costs](#term:indirect-costs) are budgeted at the organisation's federally [negotiated rate](#term:nicra) unless a [solicitation](#term:program-solicitation) says otherwise [257](#cite:257). The [15 percent cap](#term:indirect-rate-cap) NSF announced in May 2025 was [vacated](#term:vacatur) by a court and is not in effect [237](#cite:237) [238](#cite:238).
cost_sharing: Voluntary committed [cost sharing](#term:cost-sharing) is prohibited [257](#cite:257).
review: A concept outline is considered by the programme officer before a full proposal is allowed [166](#cite:166) [185](#cite:185). A declined RAPID proposal is not eligible for reconsideration [258](#cite:258). A third-party guide describes review as internal by default [264](#cite:264).
distinctive: ENG states that RAPID and EAGER are not for projects appropriate for submission as standard NSF research proposals [166](#cite:166).

pending_changes.text: [NSF](#term:nsf) has proposed to replace the [PAPPG](#term:pappg) with a Guidance on [Financial Assistance](#term:financial-assistance); comments closed August 24, 2026 and NSF's stated goal is to issue it for use in early to mid FY2027 [152](#cite:152) [151](#cite:151).

conflicts: EAGER ceiling: $400,000 in Supplement 1 [149] vs $300,000 on NSF's early-career page last updated September 26, 2025 [251](#cite:251) and in a third-party guide updated September 14, 2026 [264](#cite:264).
name: EArly-concept Grants for Exploratory Research (EAGER)
what: [EAGER](#term:eager-rapid) is a proposal type defined in PAPPG Chapter II.F for exploratory work in its early stages on untested but potentially transformative research ideas [257](#cite:257) [251](#cite:251). Supplement 1 sets the request ceiling at $400,000 for up to two years [149](#cite:149).
status_note: EAGER is a proposal type with no notice of its own; NSF 26-517 (BIO Core) states that EAGER proposals may be submitted at any time once a [concept outline](#term:concept-outline) has been submitted and NSF BIO has approved submission [185](#cite:185). The ENG proposal guidance states that EAGER proposals can be submitted at any time after a concept outline has gone to the cognizant programme director [166](#cite:166).

who_may_apply.investigator: Same organisations and investigators as any NSF proposal [156](#cite:156).
who_may_apply.limits: MPS Chemistry exempts EAGER proposals from its two-proposals-per-year limit [213](#cite:213). No general limit was found on a page read in this sweep [257](#cite:257).
who_may_apply.eligibility_note: The proposer categories of PAPPG Chapter I.E apply, which include non-profit non-academic organisations located in the U.S. [156](#cite:156).

steps: The [PI](#term:principal-investigator) submits a concept outline to NSF before an EAGER proposal [251](#cite:251).
In BIO, approval from the [directorate](#term:nsf-directorate) is required before the full proposal is submitted [185](#cite:185).
The proposal is prepared in [Research.gov](#term:research-gov) as proposal type EAGER [252](#cite:252).
An EAGER award can be renewed only through a [renewal](#term:renewal) proposal that goes through full external [merit review](#term:merit-review) [252](#cite:252).

cycle.pattern: May be submitted at any time, after a concept outline has gone to the [programme officer](#term:program-officer) [166](#cite:166) [185](#cite:185).

awards.label: request ceiling, including indirect costs (from December 8, 2025)

indirect_costs: [Indirect costs](#term:indirect-costs) are budgeted at the organisation's federally [negotiated rate](#term:nicra) unless a [solicitation](#term:program-solicitation) says otherwise [257](#cite:257). The [15 percent cap](#term:indirect-rate-cap) NSF announced in May 2025 was [vacated](#term:vacatur) by a court and is not in effect [237](#cite:237) [238](#cite:238).
cost_sharing: Voluntary committed [cost sharing](#term:cost-sharing) is prohibited [257](#cite:257).
review: NSF's early-career page says EAGER proposals are reviewed internally, which shortens the time from submission to funding [251](#cite:251). A declined EAGER proposal is not eligible for reconsideration [258](#cite:258).
distinctive: NSF describes EAGER as support for high-risk, high-reward exploratory work [251](#cite:251).

name: Research Advanced by Interdisciplinary Science and Engineering (RAISE)
what: RAISE is a proposal type defined in PAPPG Chapter II.F [257](#cite:257). NSF's 2026 core [solicitations](#term:program-solicitation) name it, with planning proposals, RAPID and [EAGER](#term:eager-rapid), as a mechanism for preliminary or time-sensitive work [212](#cite:212) [206](#cite:206).
status_note: RAISE is a proposal type with no notice of its own; NSF 26-517 (BIO Core), posted August 17, 2026, states that RAISE proposals may be submitted at any time once a [concept outline](#term:concept-outline) has been submitted and NSF BIO has approved submission [185](#cite:185).

who_may_apply.investigator: Same organisations and investigators as any NSF proposal [156](#cite:156).
who_may_apply.limits: MPS Chemistry exempts RAISE proposals from its two-proposals-per-year limit [213](#cite:213).
who_may_apply.eligibility_note: The proposer categories of PAPPG Chapter I.E apply, which include non-profit non-academic organisations located in the U.S. [156](#cite:156).

steps: The [PI](#term:principal-investigator) submits a concept outline before the proposal [185](#cite:185).
The proposal is prepared in [Research.gov](#term:research-gov) as proposal type RAISE [252](#cite:252).

cycle.pattern: May be submitted at any time after a concept outline; in BIO, [directorate](#term:nsf-directorate) approval is required first [185](#cite:185).

indirect_costs: [Indirect costs](#term:indirect-costs) are budgeted at the organisation's federally [negotiated rate](#term:nicra) unless a solicitation says otherwise [257](#cite:257). The [15 percent cap](#term:indirect-rate-cap) NSF announced in May 2025 was [vacated](#term:vacatur) by a court and is not in effect [237](#cite:237) [238](#cite:238).
cost_sharing: Voluntary committed [cost sharing](#term:cost-sharing) is prohibited [257](#cite:257).
review: A third-party guide states that the concept outline is considered by at least two [programme officers](#term:program-officer) and that review is internal by default [264](#cite:264).
distinctive: NSF's 2026 core solicitations list RAISE among the mechanisms for preliminary or time-sensitive work [212](#cite:212).

name: Grant Opportunities for Academic Liaison with Industry (GOALI)
what: GOALI is a proposal type defined in PAPPG Chapter II.F [257](#cite:257). In ENG a GOALI request may come with a regular proposal, as an [unsolicited proposal](#term:unsolicited-request), or as a supplemental funding request to an active award [166](#cite:166).
status_note: GOALI is a proposal type with no notice of its own; the ENG proposal guidance states that a GOALI proposal may be submitted in conjunction with a regular proposal to an NSF programme, as an unsolicited proposal, or as a supplemental funding request to an active award, after contact with the programme director, and it lists no proposal type as paused or discontinued [166](#cite:166).

who_may_apply.investigator: Same organisations and investigators as any NSF proposal [156](#cite:156). In ENG the [PI](#term:principal-investigator) contacts the programme director before submission [166](#cite:166).
who_may_apply.limits: A third-party guide states that limits are those of the host funding opportunity [264](#cite:264).
who_may_apply.eligibility_note: The proposer categories of PAPPG Chapter I.E apply, which include non-profit non-academic organisations located in the U.S. [156](#cite:156).

steps: The PI contacts the cognizant programme director before submission [166](#cite:166).
A GOALI proposal can be started in [Grants.gov](#term:grants-gov) but must be completed in [Research.gov](#term:research-gov) [252](#cite:252).

cycle.pattern: Follows the funding opportunity to which the GOALI proposal is sent [264](#cite:264) [166](#cite:166).

awards.label: award size and duration (secondary source only)
awards.amount: set by the host funding opportunity
awards.duration: set by the host funding opportunity

indirect_costs: [Indirect costs](#term:indirect-costs) are budgeted at the organisation's federally [negotiated rate](#term:nicra) unless a [solicitation](#term:program-solicitation) says otherwise [257](#cite:257). The [15 percent cap](#term:indirect-rate-cap) NSF announced in May 2025 was [vacated](#term:vacatur) by a court and is not in effect [237](#cite:237) [238](#cite:238).
cost_sharing: Voluntary committed [cost sharing](#term:cost-sharing) is prohibited [257](#cite:257).
review: A third-party guide states that a GOALI proposal receives the review of its host opportunity plus GOALI-specific criteria [264](#cite:264).
distinctive: ENG presents GOALI as a way to add an industry partnership to a core research proposal or an active award [166](#cite:166).

name: Planning proposal
what: The planning proposal is a proposal type defined in PAPPG Chapter II.F [257](#cite:257). Supplement 1 raised the request ceiling to $200,000 per year for up to two years [149](#cite:149).
status_note: The planning proposal is a proposal type with no notice of its own; NSF 26-517 (BIO Core), posted August 17, 2026, states that Planning proposals may be submitted at any time once a [concept outline](#term:concept-outline) has been submitted and NSF BIO has approved submission [185](#cite:185).

who_may_apply.investigator: Same organisations and investigators as any NSF proposal [156](#cite:156).
who_may_apply.limits: No general limit was found on a page read in this sweep [257](#cite:257).
who_may_apply.eligibility_note: The proposer categories of PAPPG Chapter I.E apply, which include non-profit non-academic organisations located in the U.S. [156](#cite:156).

steps: The [PI](#term:principal-investigator) submits a concept outline before the proposal [185](#cite:185).
The proposal is prepared in [Research.gov](#term:research-gov) as proposal type Planning [252](#cite:252).
A planning award can be renewed only through a [renewal](#term:renewal) proposal that goes through full external [merit review](#term:merit-review) [252](#cite:252).

cycle.pattern: May be submitted at any time after a concept outline; in BIO, [directorate](#term:nsf-directorate) approval is required first [185](#cite:185).

indirect_costs: [Indirect costs](#term:indirect-costs) are budgeted at the organisation's federally [negotiated rate](#term:nicra) unless a [solicitation](#term:program-solicitation) says otherwise [257](#cite:257). The [15 percent cap](#term:indirect-rate-cap) NSF announced in May 2025 was [vacated](#term:vacatur) by a court and is not in effect [237](#cite:237) [238](#cite:238).
cost_sharing: Voluntary committed [cost sharing](#term:cost-sharing) is prohibited [257](#cite:257).
review: A concept outline is required before submission [185](#cite:185). How planning proposals are reviewed was not found on a page read in this sweep [257](#cite:257).
distinctive: NSF's 2026 core solicitations name the planning proposal first among mechanisms for preliminary work [212](#cite:212).

name: Conference proposal
what: The conference proposal is a proposal type defined in PAPPG Chapter II.F for conferences, workshops and symposia [257](#cite:257) [212](#cite:212). The MPS Physics [solicitation](#term:program-solicitation) states that such proposals up to $200,000 need no external review [212](#cite:212).
status_note: The conference proposal is a proposal type with no notice of its own; NSF 26-517 (BIO Core) states that travel or conference support, including workshops, can be submitted at any time [185](#cite:185). The ENG proposal guidance states that conference proposals should be submitted at least a year in advance of the scheduled meeting [166](#cite:166).

who_may_apply.investigator: Same organisations and investigators as any NSF proposal [156](#cite:156). MPS Physics asks [PIs](#term:principal-investigator) to contact the programme before submitting [212](#cite:212).
who_may_apply.limits: MPS Chemistry exempts conference proposals from its two-proposals-per-year limit [213](#cite:213).
who_may_apply.eligibility_note: The proposer categories of PAPPG Chapter I.E apply, which include non-profit non-academic organisations located in the U.S. [156](#cite:156).

steps: The PI discusses objectives, agenda, location, dates, organisers and dissemination with the programme director (ENG) [166](#cite:166).
The proposal is prepared in [Research.gov](#term:research-gov) as proposal type Conference [252](#cite:252).

cycle.pattern: Accepted at any time in BIO [185](#cite:185). ENG asks for conference proposals at least a year before the meeting, and funding is at the discretion of each ENG unit [166](#cite:166).

awards.label: ceiling below which external review is not required (MPS Physics)

indirect_costs: [Indirect costs](#term:indirect-costs) are budgeted at the organisation's federally [negotiated rate](#term:nicra) unless a solicitation says otherwise [257](#cite:257). The [15 percent cap](#term:indirect-rate-cap) NSF announced in May 2025 was [vacated](#term:vacatur) by a court and is not in effect [237](#cite:237) [238](#cite:238).
cost_sharing: Voluntary committed [cost sharing](#term:cost-sharing) is prohibited [257](#cite:257).
review: External review is not required for conference, workshop or symposium proposals up to $200,000 in MPS Physics [212]. A secondary source reports that in December 2025 NSF raised a ceiling for workshop and symposium proposals from $100,000 to $200,000 [176](#cite:176).
distinctive: BIO's 2026 solicitation groups conference support with travel and workshops as requests that can arrive at any time [185](#cite:185).

name: Research in Undergraduate Institutions (RUI) and Research Opportunity Awards (ROA-PUI)
what: RUI supports faculty research at [predominantly undergraduate institutions](#term:predominantly-undergraduate-institution); ROA-PUI lets faculty from those institutions work with NSF-funded investigators elsewhere [253](#cite:253). Both run through NSF's disciplinary programmes under [solicitation](#term:program-solicitation) NSF 14-579, and the money comes from each programme's budget [253](#cite:253) [254](#cite:254).
status_note: The opportunity page lists NSF 14-579, posted July 1, 2014, as the current solicitation with "Full proposal accepted anytime" and the note that submission deadlines vary by programme [253](#cite:253). NSF 26-517 (BIO Core) states that RUI proposals may be submitted at any time and must follow the proposal preparation guidance in the RUI solicitation [185](#cite:185).

who_may_apply.investigator: The [PI](#term:principal-investigator) is a faculty member at an eligible predominantly undergraduate institution [253](#cite:253).
who_may_apply.limits: No limit per organisation; the number of proposals allowed per PI varies by programme [254](#cite:254).
who_may_apply.eligibility_note: Only predominantly undergraduate institutions qualify: accredited colleges and universities that have awarded 20 or fewer Ph.D./D.Sci. degrees in all NSF-supported fields in the previous two academic years combined [254](#cite:254). A non-profit that is not a college or university is not within that definition [254](#cite:254).

steps: The PI contacts the disciplinary [programme officer](#term:program-officer) to settle the programme and timing [253](#cite:253).
The proposal adds a Certification of RUI/ROA Eligibility and an RUI Impact Statement of no more than five pages [254](#cite:254).
ROA support is requested as a supplement to an existing NSF award, by re-budgeting an award, or within a new proposal [254](#cite:254).
The proposal is submitted through [Research.gov](#term:research-gov) or [Grants.gov](#term:grants-gov) [254](#cite:254).

cycle.pattern: Proposals are accepted at any time, subject to the deadlines of the disciplinary programme to which they are sent [254](#cite:254) [253](#cite:253).

current_notices.note: Posted July 1, 2014; opportunity page last updated May 28, 2026 [253](#cite:253).

indirect_costs: The solicitation lists [indirect cost](#term:indirect-costs) limitations as not applicable [254](#cite:254). Indirect costs are budgeted at the organisation's federally [negotiated rate](#term:nicra) unless a solicitation says otherwise [257](#cite:257). The [15 percent cap](#term:indirect-rate-cap) NSF announced in May 2025 was [vacated](#term:vacatur) by a court and is not in effect [237](#cite:237) [238](#cite:238).
cost_sharing: Inclusion of voluntary committed [cost sharing](#term:cost-sharing) is prohibited [254](#cite:254).
review: Proposals are judged on the two National Science Board criteria, [Intellectual Merit and Broader Impacts](#term:intellectual-merit) [157](#cite:157). An RUI proposal goes to a disciplinary programme and carries an RUI Impact Statement of up to five pages as an extra document [254](#cite:254).
distinctive: NSF states that RUI and ROA funds are not a separate allocation but sit within individual programme budgets [253](#cite:253).

pending_changes.text: [NSF](#term:nsf) has proposed to replace the [PAPPG](#term:pappg) with a Guidance on [Financial Assistance](#term:financial-assistance); comments closed August 24, 2026 and NSF's stated goal is to issue it for use in early to mid FY2027 [152](#cite:152) [151](#cite:151).

name: Core Research in Biological Sciences (BIO Core)
what: BIO Core is the single [solicitation](#term:program-solicitation) for foundational research across biology, in three thematic areas: Foundations of Life, Living Systems, and Bioinnovation and Infrastructure [185](#cite:185) [184](#cite:184).
status_note: The opportunity page lists NSF 26-517 as the current solicitation with "Full proposal accepted anytime" [2521](#cite:2521). The solicitation itself gives "Proposals Accepted Anytime" in place of a deadline and states that it replaces NSF 24-543, NSF 24-546 and NSF 24-539 [185](#cite:185).

who_may_apply.investigator: The solicitation states no restrictions or limits on who may serve as [PI](#term:principal-investigator) [185](#cite:185).
who_may_apply.limits: No limit on proposals per organisation or per PI or [co-PI](#term:multiple-pi) [185](#cite:185).
who_may_apply.eligibility_note: The solicitation names [institutions of higher education](#term:institution-of-higher-education), non-profit non-academic organisations and Tribal Nations as eligible proposers [185](#cite:185). A non-profit that is not a university may apply if it is a U.S. organisation directly associated with educational or research activities [156](#cite:156).

steps: The applicant reads the solicitation and contacts a [programme officer](#term:program-officer) listed on the opportunity [185](#cite:185) [158](#cite:158).

RAPID, [EAGER](#term:eager-rapid), RAISE and planning proposals to BIO need a [concept outline](#term:concept-outline) and BIO's approval first; RUI proposals follow the RUI solicitation; CAREER proposals follow the CAREER solicitation [185](#cite:185).
The organisation holds an active [SAM registration](#term:sam-gov) and a [UEI](#term:uei) before submission [156](#cite:156).
The proposal follows PAPPG 24-1 as amended by its two [supplements](#term:supplement) [147](#cite:147).
The proposal is submitted through [Research.gov](#term:research-gov) or [Grants.gov](#term:grants-gov) [185](#cite:185).
NSF aims to tell the applicant the outcome within six months [160](#cite:160).

cycle.pattern: Proposals are accepted at any time; there is no deadline [185](#cite:185).

current_notices.note: Posted 2026-08-17; it replaces NSF 24-543, NSF 24-546 and NSF 24-539 [185](#cite:185).

awards.label: project period encouraged
awards.duration: up to five years of support

indirect_costs: The solicitation lists [indirect cost](#term:indirect-costs) (F&A) limitations as not applicable [185](#cite:185). Indirect costs are budgeted at the organisation's federally [negotiated rate](#term:nicra) unless a solicitation says otherwise [257](#cite:257). The [15 percent cap](#term:indirect-rate-cap) NSF announced in May 2025 was [vacated](#term:vacatur) by a court and is not in effect [237](#cite:237) [238](#cite:238).
cost_sharing: Inclusion of voluntary committed [cost sharing](#term:cost-sharing) is prohibited [185](#cite:185).
review: Proposals are judged on the two National Science Board criteria, [Intellectual Merit and Broader Impacts](#term:intellectual-merit) [157](#cite:157). Review is by ad hoc review and/or panel review, or internal NSF review; the solicitation says that in most cases three or more external experts also review a proposal [185](#cite:185).
distinctive: BIO describes the opportunity as supporting foundational research across all areas of biology [184](#cite:184).

name: CISE Future Computing Research (Future CoRe)
what: Future CoRe is the CISE core-research [solicitation](#term:program-solicitation), covering eleven programmes from Algorithmic Foundations to Software and Hardware Foundations [189](#cite:189). It was posted in July 2025 and is the current solicitation on the live opportunity page [190](#cite:190).
status_note: The opportunity page lists NSF 25-543 as the current solicitation and states that proposals are accepted anytime, with target dates of February 4, 2027 (first Thursday in February, annually thereafter) and September 9, 2027 (second Thursday in September, annually thereafter) [190](#cite:190).

who_may_apply.investigator: The solicitation states no restrictions or limits on who may serve as [PI](#term:principal-investigator) [189](#cite:189).
who_may_apply.limits: There is no limit per organisation, and an individual may be PI, [co-PI](#term:multiple-pi) or senior/key personnel on no more than two proposals in any consecutive 12-month period across the Future CoRe programmes [189](#cite:189) [190](#cite:190).
who_may_apply.eligibility_note: The solicitation names [institutions of higher education](#term:institution-of-higher-education), non-profit non-academic organisations and Tribal Nations as eligible proposers [189](#cite:189). A non-profit that is not a university may apply if it is a U.S. organisation directly associated with educational or research activities [156](#cite:156).

steps: The applicant reads the solicitation and contacts a [programme officer](#term:program-officer) listed on the opportunity [189](#cite:189) [158](#cite:158).
The organisation holds an active [SAM registration](#term:sam-gov) and a [UEI](#term:uei) before submission [156](#cite:156).
The proposal follows PAPPG 24-1 as amended by its two [supplements](#term:supplement) [147](#cite:147).
The proposal is submitted through [Research.gov](#term:research-gov) or [Grants.gov](#term:grants-gov) [189](#cite:189).
NSF aims to tell the applicant the outcome within six months [160](#cite:160).

cycle.pattern: Proposals are accepted at any time, with target dates on the second Thursday in September and the first Thursday in February each year; the next are February 4, 2027 and September 9, 2027 [189](#cite:189) [190](#cite:190).

current_notices.note: Posted 2025-07-25; it replaces NSF 24-589, NSF 24-581 and NSF 25-527 [189](#cite:189).

indirect_costs: The solicitation lists [indirect cost](#term:indirect-costs) (F&A) limitations as not applicable [189](#cite:189). Indirect costs are budgeted at the organisation's federally [negotiated rate](#term:nicra) unless a solicitation says otherwise [257](#cite:257). The [15 percent cap](#term:indirect-rate-cap) NSF announced in May 2025 was [vacated](#term:vacatur) by a court and is not in effect [237](#cite:237) [238](#cite:238).
cost_sharing: Inclusion of voluntary committed [cost sharing](#term:cost-sharing) is prohibited [189](#cite:189).
review: Proposals are judged on the two National Science Board criteria, [Intellectual Merit and Broader Impacts](#term:intellectual-merit) [157](#cite:157). The solicitation ties consideration to panel review cycles that follow each target date [189](#cite:189).
distinctive: The solicitation says proposals are accepted anytime but encourages submission by the target dates so that they reach the matching panel cycle [189](#cite:189).
