name: Expeditions in Computing
what: Expeditions funds large multidisciplinary teams pursuing ambitious, foundational research agendas in computing [191](#cite:191). It was reissued on August 17, 2026 as one of NSF's twelve foundational-research notices [192](#cite:192).
status_note: The opportunity page lists NSF 26-525 as the current [solicitation](#term:program-solicitation), with [preliminary proposals](#term:pre-application) due December 2, 2026 and a full proposal deadline of July 27, 2027 [2522](#cite:2522).

who_may_apply.investigator: An individual may take part in one preliminary and one full proposal per competition [191](#cite:191).
who_may_apply.limits: An individual may participate in no more than one preliminary proposal and, if invited, one full proposal per competition [191](#cite:191).
who_may_apply.eligibility_note: Eligible proposers are U.S. [institutions of higher education](#term:institution-of-higher-education) with accredited undergraduate, master's and doctoral programmes in computer and information science fields [191](#cite:191). The fetched text names no non-profit non-academic category [191](#cite:191).

name: Office of Science annual open funding opportunity (FY 2027 Continuation of Solicitation for the Office of Science Financial Assistance Program)
what: The Office of Science keeps one funding notice open all year for research proposals in the fields of its programme offices. The FY 2027 notice is DE-FOA-0003665, posted September 30, 2026 and open until September 30, 2027 or until a successor notice replaces it [277](#cite:277). It covers Advanced Scientific Computing Research, Basic Energy Sciences, Biological and Environmental Research, Fusion Energy Sciences, High Energy Physics, Isotope R&D and Production, and Nuclear Physics [277](#cite:277). DOE calls the notice a [NOFO](#term:nofo) (notice of funding opportunity); it is issued in two parts, Part 1 with the programme content and Part 2 with fixed DOE requirements [278](#cite:278) [279](#cite:279).
status_note: The notice page for DE-FOA-0003665 gives a post date of Wednesday, September 30, 2026 and a close date of Thursday, September 30, 2027, and states that the notice will remain open until September 30, 2027, or until replaced by a successor; applications may be submitted at any time during the open period [277](#cite:277).

who_may_apply.investigator: Individuals not affiliated with a research institution may apply if the application shows they have the skills, abilities and resources; no career-stage rule was found in the parts read [278](#cite:278). Non-domestic applicants are to include a detailed demonstration of their skills, resources and abilities [278](#cite:278). DOE/NNSA national laboratories may not apply under this notice but may be proposed as [subrecipients](#term:subrecipient) [278](#cite:278). Entities of Concern may not take part [278](#cite:278).
who_may_apply.limits: No limit on the number of applications per applicant is stated [278](#cite:278).

The programme manager recommends funding, senior officials concur, and the Integrated Service Center negotiates and issues the award [364](#cite:364).

name: ARPA-E programme funding notices
what: ARPA-E issues a notice for each focused technology programme and funds teams by [cooperative agreement](#term:cooperative-agreement), with other transactions in some cases [301](#cite:301). A notice runs in three stages: a [concept paper](#term:concept-outline), a full application, and a reply to reviewer comments [301](#cite:301). The CATALCHEM-E notice (DE-FOA-0003505), issued November 14, 2024 and modified February 6, 2026, is used here as the worked example [301](#cite:301).
status_note: Two ARPA-E listings were re-read and neither is a notice in force for a new applicant: SCALEUP Ready (DE-FOA-0003467) is Open, posted October 2, 2024 and closing September 29, 2029, and is for technologies ARPA-E has already funded, while IGNIITE 2026 (DE-FOA-0003624) is Closed, posted April 23, 2026 with a closing date of August 26, 2026 [370](#cite:370) [304](#cite:304). The ARPA-E exchange address returned only a notice that the site has been decommissioned and consolidated into eXCHANGE.energy.gov, so the full list of current programme notices was not read within the three fetches allowed [305](#cite:305).
status_change: The ARPA-E exchange at arpa-e-foa.energy.gov now shows a decommissioning notice pointing to eXCHANGE.energy.gov and lists no opportunities [305](#cite:305).

who_may_apply.investigator: In the example notice, domestic for-profit and non-profit organisations, educational institutions, FFRDCs and DOE laboratories may apply; foreign entities are not eligible applicants but may take part as subcontractors; non-profits described in section 501(c)(4) are not eligible [301](#cite:301). A 2026 ARPA-E notice required a Foreign Entity Waiver for foreign participation [304](#cite:304). Only U.S. citizens or permanent residents may apply in an individual capacity [302](#cite:302).
who_may_apply.limits: Not found in the parts read [301](#cite:301).

steps: Register in [SAM](#term:sam-gov) and obtain a [Unique Entity Identifier](#term:uei); create an eXCHANGE account [301](#cite:301).
Submit a concept paper by the notice's date [301](#cite:301).
Submit a full application; ARPA-E then releases reviewer comments [301](#cite:301).
Submit a reply to reviewer comments by the stated date [301](#cite:301).
ARPA-E notifies applicants and negotiates awards [301](#cite:301).

indirect_costs: Modification 03 of the example notice, dated February 6, 2026, removed a cap on [indirect costs](#term:indirect-costs) at 15% of total project costs [301](#cite:301). A second ARPA-E notice records the same removal [302](#cite:302).
cost_sharing: The base requirement in the example notice is at least 20% of total project costs, with a reduced requirement of 10% for small businesses, for educational institutions or domestic non-profits applying alone, and for teams made up of or mostly of such entities [301](#cite:301). A 2019–2020 ARPA-E notice required no cost share from a domestic university or non-profit applying alone [400](#cite:400). The regulation sets 20 percent for research and development and 50 percent for demonstration and commercial application [299](#cite:299).
review: Concept papers and full applications are reviewed against criteria printed in each notice [301](#cite:301). In the OPEN 2018 notice the full-application criteria were weighted: impact of the proposed technology 30%, overall scientific and technical merit 30%, qualifications, experience and capabilities 30%, soundness of management plan 10% [303](#cite:303).
distinctive: In the example notice at least 5% of federal funding goes to technology transfer and outreach, and work is to be performed in the United States unless waived [301](#cite:301).

It can lead to a [grant](#term:grant), a [cooperative agreement](#term:cooperative-agreement), a contract or an other transaction agreement [334](#cite:334). steps: Submit a pre-application through [Grants.gov](#term:grants-gov) by the deadline (June 15, 2026 for FY 2026) [414](#cite:414).

owner: USDA National Institute of Food and Agriculture

what: National Leadership Grants for Libraries fund projects that develop, enhance or adapt replicable practices, programmes, models or tools to strengthen library and archival services [676](#cite:676) [677](#cite:677). eligibility_note: The foundation says the vast majority of this funding goes to non-profit organisations and public agencies, and less than 1 percent historically to for-profit companies. A non-profit that is not a university may apply [2336](#cite:2336).

cycle.pattern: The call closes each year on or about October 15 and reopens on or about February 1 [2336](#cite:2336). The dates for the 2026 round were not confirmed on a page dated 2026 [2336](#cite:2336).

awards.label: typical award in 2023
awards.duration: 2 to 3 years on average; no fixed cap on amount or duration

indirect_costs: Allowed; the rate 'varies by type of organization' under the foundation's [indirect cost](#term:indirect-costs) policy [2336](#cite:2336).

success.note: 8 grants from the applications received in 2024; the foundation says 600 to 1,000 submissions arrive each year [2336](#cite:2336).

name: Evidence for Action: Rapid Response Research
what: A single call issued in August 2025 to 'Support timely, actionable health equity research that has been interrupted by shifts in federal funding' [2337](#cite:2337). Applicants had to have lost federal funding for a health equity research project and document the [termination](#term:termination) [2337](#cite:2337).

who_may_apply.limits: Organisations only, based in the United States [2337](#cite:2337).

steps: Submit a brief proposal in the foundation's online system [2337](#cite:2337).
eligibility_note: Universities, non-profits and research institutions were eligible; a non-profit that is not a university could apply [2337](#cite:2337).

cycle.pattern: One deadline; no later round was found [2337](#cite:2337).

current_notices.note: Brief proposals were due October 1, 2025 at 3 p.m. ET; applicants were to be notified the week of November 17, 2025, for [grants](#term:grant) starting January 15, 2026 [2337](#cite:2337).

indirect_costs: Grant funds 'will also cover [indirect costs](#term:indirect-costs)'; no rate is given in the call [2337](#cite:2337).

name: Mellon Higher Learning Program Open Call for Concepts
what: An [open call](#term:open-call) from the foundation's Higher Learning programme for research and curricular projects in the humanities on set themes; the 2026 themes were 'Unruly Intelligences' and 'Normalization and Its Discontents' [2339](#cite:2339). The foundation committed $10 million to the 2026 call [2339](#cite:2339).

who_may_apply.limits: 'Each institution may submit no more than three applications to Mellon for consideration.' [2339](#cite:2339)

steps: Register in Mellon's Fluxx [grants](#term:grant) portal by the registration deadline [2339](#cite:2339).
Submit the application in the portal by the application deadline [2339](#cite:2339).
eligibility_note: Only accredited, non-profit, four-year degree-granting institutions in the United States and its territories with at least 1,000 full-time undergraduates may apply. Research institutes, fully online institutions and special-focus institutions are not eligible, so a non-profit that is not such a college or university may not apply [2339](#cite:2339).

cycle.pattern: The 2026 call is closed; whether a call for 2027 will be held was not found [2339](#cite:2339).

current_notices.note: Registration was due December 1, 2025 and applications February 17, 2026, both at 3:00 p.m. ET, with notification in summer 2026 [2339](#cite:2339).

name: Arnold Ventures request for proposals: Causal Research on the Impacts of K-12 School Policies
what: A [request for proposals](#term:open-call) issued in September 2026 for causal studies of the effects of K-12 school policies [2321](#cite:2321) [2318](#cite:2318). It is one of two requests listed as open on 2026-10-04 [2318](#cite:2318).
steps: Submit a letter of interest by November 13, 2026 [2321](#cite:2321).
If invited, submit a full proposal by January 31, 2027 [2321](#cite:2321).
eligibility_note: The request states no restriction by type of organisation, so it does not shut out a non-profit that is not a university [2321](#cite:2321).

cycle.pattern: Two steps on fixed dates [2321](#cite:2321).

current_notices.note: Letters of interest are due November 13, 2026; invitations to submit a full proposal follow on December 18, 2026; full proposals are due January 31, 2027; notification of award is estimated for March 31, 2027 [2321](#cite:2321).

review: Two criteria: policy relevance and causal study design [2321](#cite:2321).
